title: Justifiable Priority Violations
abstract: arXiv:2604.06396v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Making Deferred Acceptance more efficient requires priority violations, but which ones are justifiable? We argue that a priority can be justifiably violated if the affected student either (i) directly benefits from the improvement that caused said violation, or (ii) is unimprovable under any assignment that Pareto-dominates DA. We construct a ``just-below-cutoffs'' mechanism that always finds a justifiable DA-improvement whenever DA's outcome is inefficient, and build on it to construct an algorithm that expands justifiable improvements iteratively, converging to a matching that cannot be Pareto-improved by any justifiable outcome. Finally, we prove that both justifiability and consent frameworks have important limitations in reaching Pareto-efficient outcomes, and use data and simulations to quantify how binding these constraints are in practice.

translated_title: 可正当化的优先权违背
translated_abstract: 让延迟接受机制更有效率就需要优先权违背，但哪些违背是正当的呢？我们认为，如果受影响的学生满足以下条件之一，其优先权就可以被正当地违背： 该学生直接从导致该违背的改进中受益； 在任何帕累托优于延迟接受（DA）结果的分配中，该学生的处境都无法被改进。我们构建了一个“刚好低于截止线”机制，只要DA的结果是非有效的，该机制总能找到一个正当的DA改进；并在此基础上构建了一种算法，迭代地扩展正当的改进，最终收敛到一个无法被任何正当结果帕累托改进的匹配。最后，我们证明了正当性框架和同意框架在达到帕累托有效结果方面均存在重要局限，并利用数据和模拟来量化这些约束在实践中的约束力。
tldr: 该论文提出了“可正当化优先权违背”的新标准——受影响学生要么直接受益于导致违背的改进，要么在任何帕累托优于DA的分配中都无法被改进——并据此构建了“刚好低于截止线”机制和迭代算法以持续改进DA结果，同时揭示了正当性与同意框架在实现帕累托效率上的根本局限。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces "justifiable priority violations"—where the affected student either directly benefits from the causing improvement or is unimprovable under any DA-dominating assignment—constructs a "just-below-cutoffs" mechanism and an iterative algorithm that converges to a matching not Pareto-improvable by any justifiable outcome, and proves fundamental limitations of justifiability and consent frameworks in achieving Pareto efficiency.
